- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward moves (spikes) — apply a “lag correction”: if true outcome shows a spike, forecast should be adjusted up by 1–2% of the spike magnitude.  
- Model tends to overestimate downward moves — apply “mean reversion” rule: if forecast dips below 10% of recent 5-day average, gently push back toward that average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses the “late-cycle” rally — if sentiment turns positive after 15–20 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +1, -2, +1), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to match sentiment’s direction 1–2 days ahead.
